subject: Private pin orchestration: escape-hatch, network drain, and staged rollback
messages:
From: Sandra Li <sandra.li@acme.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Request: private maintenance window + pin/rollback guidance

Hi Sean,

We're planning an internal maintenance window to accept your team's private deployment patch (minor upgrade) and want to align on how Redwood will handle version pinning and an escape hatch. A couple of constraints from our security and platform teams: 

- We need a documented rollback plan and an expected RTO if we have to revert.
- Network drain choreography is required (cordon/drain + session handoff).
- Any KMS/HSM key rotations must be non-disruptive to ongoing inference requests or clearly documented.

Can you confirm:
1) Whether Redwood supports a fast 'shelve' back to the previously pinned LTS version if the patch causes regressions?
2) Recommended maintenance window length and recommended drain timeout values for a typical ~200 qps workload?
3) A preflight checklist we can use for our ops runbook (we attached our request).

We'd like to schedule a 2–3 hour window next week (Thu/Fri) if possible. Please loop in anyone from your infra team who should be present.

Thanks,
Sandra
Sandra Li
Senior Engineer, Platform
Acme Corp

Attachments: acme_maintenance_request.pdf

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Sandra Li <sandra.li@acme.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 12:40:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: private maintenance window + pin/rollback guidance

Hi Sandra — thanks for the clear asks. Below is a concise plan we use for Private (VPC/on-prem) upgrades that should address your items.

High-level approach
- Pinning model: we pin deployments at the model/runtime image level. For this patch we'll pin to runtime v2.14.1 in a phased canary rollout and keep v2.12.8 (LTS) available as the escape hatch.
- Escape hatch ("shelve"): we support an automated shelve operation: rebind routes to the LTS variant + publish a temporary no-new-sessions policy. That operation restores previous binaries within ~3–7 minutes for a typical fleet size.
- Network drain choreography: cordon nodes, quick connection handoff in the proxy layer, allow in-flight tokens to finish (recommended drain timeout = 120s), then perform instance restart.

Proposed schedule
- Preflight dry run: Wed 06/30 10:00–11:00 PDT (no traffic) — run healthchecks + smoke tests
- Maintenance window (live): Thu 07/01 02:00–05:00 PDT — 3-hour block to allow canaries, ramp, and validation

Rollback and abort criteria
- Abort immediately if 5xx rate increases >1.5x baseline for 10m or if latency P95 increases >40% on any canary shard.
- Immediate rollback: trigger shelve to v2.12.8, disable autoscale up for 30m.
- Recovery verification: smoke endpoints + kv-cache integrity check + perf sanity queries.

Operational artifacts (attached)
- se an-pinning-runbook-v1.md: run steps, CLI commands (redwoodctl pin/shelve), and preflight checklist
- network-drain-checklist.xlsx: step-by-step for cordon/drain and proxy handoff

People to join
- Sean Gallagher (ops lead)
- Monica Patel (infrastructure, will own KV cache validation)
- Aditya Rao (on-call runtime engineer)

Next steps
1) Confirm the proposed window (Thu 07/01 02:00–05:00 PDT).
2) Share any additional audit gating items and we'll embed them into the runbook.

Cheers,
Sean Gallagher
Head of Reliability, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0192

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 08:30:47 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: private maintenance window + pin/rollback guidance

Sandra — quick technical clarifications from infra before we lock the window. I quoted Sean's plan inline for context.

On Tue, Jun 23, 2026 at 12:40 PM Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com> wrote:
> - Escape hatch ("shelve"): we support an automated shelve operation: rebind routes to the LTS variant + publish a temporary no-new-sessions policy. That operation restores previous binaries within ~3–7 minutes for a typical fleet size.

Notes and clarifications
- KV cache and in-flight requests: the shelve sequence will rebind new requests to LTS, but in-flight KV cache entries may reference newer quantization artifacts. Our recommended safe pattern: after shelve, do a rolling cache flush per shard (graceful flush) and monitor cache hit-rate. We will provide scripts to validate key mismatch errors.
- KMS interactions: we do not rotate customer-managed keys during this operation. If you plan a KMS rotation, please schedule that outside the maintenance window. If rotation must occur, we need a 24h pre-notice to validate decryption paths.
- Drain timeout: for 200 qps we recommend 120s drain + 60s post-drain validation before restarting instances. If you have long-running streaming sessions, bump drain to 300s and we will quiesce the endpoints first.
- Healthcheck sequence: 1) /health/live, 2) /health/ready, 3) smoke generation against pinned model (10 sample prompts). We'll publish expected thresholds in the runbook.

Operational hooks (commands)
- redwoodctl pin set --deployment <id> --image runtime:v2.14.1
- redwoodctl shelve --deployment <id> --target-image runtime:v2.12.8 --force-if-critical
- rollout-monitor --watch deployment:<id> --window 15m

Attachments: I pushed a small tar with helpers and the rollback-scripts.tar.gz for your ops: these contain the cache-flush and healthcheck wrappers.

I'll be on the call during the window. If we see any data-integrity alerts we escalate to Aditya and Sean.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Staff Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com

Attachments: rollback-scripts.tar.gz
